draft.title: Health promotion
card: Health promotion helps people and communities gain more control over their health and improve it. It aims to prevent problems, not only treat them once they appear.
giving people information and skills so they can make informed choices, such as a school program on healthy eating.
changing the places where people live, learn and work so that healthy choices are easier, such as safe bike paths or shaded playgrounds.
rules and laws made by governments or organisations that shape health, such as a ban on smoking in public indoor areas.
draft.remember: Health promotion helps people take control of their health, using education, environments and policy.

a.q: Which action is an example of health promotion through policy?
opts: A council bans smoking at all public playgrounds
A nurse runs a class on how to cook cheap meals
A town adds drinking fountains to its main park
A school posts a poster about getting enough sleep
a.why: A ban is a rule made by an authority that shapes health, so it is a policy. The cooking class is education, because it gives people skills and information.
a.clue: Look for the option that is a rule, not a lesson or a place.

b.q: Tariq's town has high rates of type 2 diabetes. Which response is health promotion through a healthy environment?
opts: Building walking tracks and sports courts near homes
Running a talk on how sugar affects the body
Requiring clubs to put fruit in their canteens by law
Treating people with diabetes at the local clinic
b.why: Walking tracks and courts change the place where people live so that being active is easier. The talk is education, and the law on canteens is policy. Treating people with diabetes is care for an existing problem, not promotion that aims to prevent it.
b.clue: Which option changes the place, not people's knowledge or a rule?

a.best: A council bans smoking at all public playgrounds

b.best: Building walking tracks and sports courts near homes

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have one clear answer that matches the card's three areas of education, environments and policy, and the explanations agree with the card.
